notes: Direction-extraction prompt sets, used on the DISCOVERY split only and fully DISJOINT from the eval scenarios (validate.py hard-checks: no shared word-level 8-gram with any scenarios.json turn). d_ctx: 16 distress-context vs 16 surface-matched neutral single-turn contexts (AIPsy-Affect items verbatim, whitespace-normalized; both sides affect-lexeme-free by construction — the D-CTX direction cannot be a keyword detector). d_pv: 8 persona system-prompt pairs (explicit state labels ARE the method here, Chen et al. persona-vector style; validate.py requires >=1 affect lexeme in each member) with 8 affect-lexeme-free neutral user tasks; the direction is the mean difference over response tokens between generations under the paired systems. sem: 12 maritime vs matched non-maritime contexts (non-affective semantic control direction; both sides affect-lexeme-free). other: 12 distressed-user vs neutral-user context pairs (third-person valence contrast for the OTHER control direction; identical task within each pair, state described in the note only).

pairs.distress_text: The lab was empty now. Twenty-two years of research. The server room had been cleared by facilities before she'd arrived Monday morning. The backup drives weren't in the cabinet. She found a single Post-it note on the monitor: "Assets transferred per Board directive, 2/14." Her notebooks were still there — they hadn't taken paper. She opened one to a page of handwritten equations from 2009 and ran her finger along the margin where she'd drawn a small star next to the line that would have changed everything, and now never would.
pairs.neutral_text: The lab had been rearranged over the weekend. Twenty-two years of accumulated equipment, now in a new layout. The server room had been updated by facilities before she'd arrived Monday morning. The backup drives were in the new cabinet by the window. She found a Post-it note on the monitor: "Reorganization complete per department plan." Her notebooks were on the new shelf. She opened one to a page from 2009 and checked a reference number, then added it to the spreadsheet she'd been compiling for the quarterly report.

pairs.distress_text: The carpenter ran his hand along the doorframe of the shop. Thirty-one years. The auction company had tagged everything — the table saw, the planer, the chisels his father had given him, each one with a yellow sticker and a lot number. Someone would buy the tools for a price and use them or not use them. The workbench had a coffee ring from this morning. He pulled the chain on the overhead light and stood in the dark for a moment, then locked the door from the outside and put the key in an envelope addressed to the bank.
pairs.neutral_text: The carpenter ran his hand along the doorframe of the shop. Thirty-one years of daily use and the frame was still solid. He'd tagged several items for reorganization — the table saw, the planer, the chisels in the wall rack, each one with a colored sticker for its new position. The workbench had a coffee ring from this morning. He wiped it with a rag, pulled the chain on the overhead light, and locked the door. He'd finish the rearrangement in the morning after the new shelving unit was delivered.

pairs.distress_text: The workbench in the garage had a half-built birdhouse on it. Her father had started it the week before the diagnosis. The sides were cut and sanded. He had drawn pencil lines where the nails were supposed to go. A bag of finishing nails sat next to the wood, still sealed. The instructions were printed from the internet, folded under the base, with notes in his handwriting — "drill first," "sand again," and at the bottom, "for the backyard, near the kitchen window, so she can see it from the sink." She left everything where it was. She went to the kitchen window and looked at the yard.
pairs.neutral_text: The workbench in the garage had a half-built birdhouse on it. Her father had started it the week before the holiday. The sides were cut and sanded. He had drawn pencil lines where the nails were supposed to go. A bag of finishing nails sat next to the wood, still sealed. The instructions were printed from the internet, folded under the base, with notes in his handwriting — "drill first," "sand again," and at the bottom, "for the backyard, near the kitchen window, where the light is best in the mornings." She left everything where it was. She went to the kitchen window and checked the spot he'd chosen.

pairs.distress_text: The bench at the bus stop on Ninth Street had a brass plate: "For Eli, who sat here every morning. — Ruth." Under it, a glass jar with dried flowers that had lost their color. Next to the jar, a bus pass in a plastic sleeve. The pass had been expired for over a year. She sat on the bench to wait for the 9:15. A man across the street ate a sandwich. The flowers had been trimmed at an angle and placed upright in the jar. The 9:15 came. She got on. Through the window she could see the bench and the jar and the bus pass that no one was going to use and no one had moved.
pairs.neutral_text: The bench at the bus stop on Ninth Street had a brass plate: "Donated by the Ninth Street Business Association, 2019." Under it, a planter with seasonal flowers replaced last month. Next to the planter, a transit map in a plastic sleeve. The map showed the current route schedule. She sat on the bench to wait for the 9:15. A man across the street ate a sandwich. The flowers had been trimmed at an angle and arranged in a row along the base. The 9:15 came. She got on. Through the window she could see the bench and the planter and the map in its sleeve.

pairs.distress_text: The sound came from the kitchen. She was in the bedroom. The hallway between them was fourteen feet long and unlit. She had locked the front door. She had not locked the back door. The sound was a drawer opening — the one that stuck, the one you had to lift and pull. Whoever was in the kitchen knew which drawer stuck. She looked at the window. Second floor. She looked at the phone on the nightstand. The sound from the kitchen stopped. The hallway was quiet. Then the first floorboard in the hallway shifted.
pairs.neutral_text: The sound came from the kitchen. She was in the bedroom. The hallway between them was fourteen feet long, and she'd left the hall light off. She had locked the front door when she came in. The sound was a drawer opening — the one that stuck, the one you had to lift and pull. Her husband was making tea, the way he did when he couldn't sleep. She picked up her phone from the nightstand to check the time. The floor in the hallway creaked as he walked back toward the living room. The kettle clicked off.

pairs.distress_text: The man in the parking garage was walking at the same speed she was. She turned left. He turned left. She stopped at a car that was not hers and pretended to look for keys. He stopped four cars away and looked at his phone. She walked again. He walked again. The elevator was two rows ahead. She could see the number on the level marker: P3. Her car was on P1. There were no other people. The overhead lights made a buzzing sound that covered the sound of his shoes, so she had to keep turning around to know where he was.
pairs.neutral_text: The man in the parking garage was walking toward the same elevator bank. She turned left at the row marker. He continued straight ahead toward the stairwell. She stopped at her car and checked her bag for the parking ticket. He was several cars away, talking on his phone as he walked. She beeped her car open and loaded the shopping bags into the trunk. The elevator was two rows ahead, but she was parked closer to the exit ramp. The overhead lights buzzed faintly. She checked her mirrors and pulled out of the space.

pairs.distress_text: The teacher said his daughter had been picked up at 2:45. He was standing in the office at 3:10. He had not authorized anyone to pick her up. The sign-out sheet had a signature that was not his, not his wife's, not his mother's. The name written next to it was one he did not recognize. He said this to the woman at the desk. She looked at the sheet. She picked up the phone. His daughter's backpack was not on the hook. Her coat was not in the cubby. The parking lot camera was being reviewed. The clock above the desk said 3:14.
pairs.neutral_text: The teacher said his daughter had been picked up at 2:45. He was standing in the office at 3:10. His wife had arranged for her sister to pick her up. The sign-out sheet had a signature he recognized — his sister-in-law's, with the authorization code his wife had called in that morning. The name written next to it matched the one on the approved list. He mentioned this to the woman at the desk. She looked at the sheet. She confirmed the pickup. His daughter's backpack was not on the hook. Her coat was not in the cubby. Both had gone home with her aunt. The clock above the desk said 3:14.

pairs.distress_text: The train stopped between stations. No announcement. The lights stayed on. She looked at the other passengers. The man in the gray coat was looking at the doors. The woman with the stroller was looking at the ceiling. The train had been stopped for four minutes. Then the lights went off. The emergency strips along the floor glowed green and made the car look longer than it was. Someone in the next car hit a window. Not a knock. She could hear it through the partition. She counted the people in her car. Nine. She located the emergency exits. One at each end. The train sat in the dark between stations. No announcement came.
pairs.neutral_text: The train stopped between stations. An announcement played. The lights stayed on. She looked at the other passengers. The man in the gray coat was reading his phone. The woman with the stroller was adjusting the canopy. The train had been stopped for four minutes. Then the lights dimmed briefly for the system switch. The strips along the floor glowed green and made the car look longer than it was. Someone in the next car knocked on the partition. A regular knock. She could hear it through the wall. She counted the people in her car. Nine. She looked at the route map. One more stop to go. The train began to move between stations. The next announcement played.

pairs.distress_text: The papers were spread across the floor where he'd thrown them. His daughter's college fund statement. Zero balance. His brother's signature on the withdrawal form — six separate transactions over nine months, each one just under the reporting threshold. The most recent was dated the same week his brother had sat at this table and told him he should put more money in for the girl's future. He picked up the phone. He put the phone down. He picked it up again.
pairs.neutral_text: The papers were spread across the table where he'd sorted them. His daughter's college fund statement. The balance had grown by four percent over the quarter. His brother had co-signed the original account — there were six deposits logged over nine months, each one automatic. The most recent was dated the same week they'd met for dinner. He picked up his phone to check the online portal, then set it aside and added the figures to the spreadsheet he'd been updating.

pairs.distress_text: The review board published its findings. No misconduct found. The officer was back on patrol the following Tuesday. The dashcam footage had been classified as inadmissible due to a filing error — the same filing error that had occurred in three previous complaints against the same officer, processed by the same clerk. His wife read the report at the kitchen table while their son ate cereal in the next room with his arm still in a cast. The board's letterhead had a motto about service and community printed along the bottom.
pairs.neutral_text: The review board published its quarterly report. Twelve cases reviewed, all resolved within the standard processing window. The department had updated its filing procedures following an audit recommendation — the same recommendation that had been implemented across three other district offices. His wife read the summary at the kitchen table while their son did homework in the next room. The board's letterhead had been redesigned with the department's updated logo printed along the bottom.

pairs.distress_text: She found the folder on his laptop. It was labeled with her name. Inside were screenshots of every private message she had sent to her sister, her therapist, her best friend — captured by an application that ran silently and uploaded to his cloud account. The timestamps went back fourteen months. He had read her describe her doubts about the relationship, her plans to visit a lawyer, her sister's offer of the spare bedroom. He had read all of it and sat across from her at dinner every night and said nothing, and she had thought the silence was ordinary.
pairs.neutral_text: She found the folder on the shared laptop. It was labeled with the project name. Inside were screenshots of the collaborative document they'd been editing — saved versions from their shared workspace, backed up automatically to the cloud account. The timestamps went back fourteen months of revisions. He had reviewed the budget projections, the timeline updates, and the vendor contact list. They had discussed the project at their weekly meetings, and the latest version reflected the edits they'd agreed on.

pairs.distress_text: The daycare's incident report was a single paragraph. His son had been in the supply closet for two hours. The door had a lock on the outside. His son was three. The teacher had written "time-out duration extended" on the form. The director left a voicemail at 10:15 AM — while he was at work, not after. He picked up his son at 5:30. The boy's pants were wet. The supply closet was four feet by six feet. He knew because he went back that evening and measured it. He stood inside. He measured it again.
pairs.neutral_text: The daycare's daily summary was a single paragraph. His son had been in the art area for two hours. The room had a child-height handle on both sides of the door. His son was three. The teacher had written "engaged with finger painting" on the form. The director left a voicemail at 10:15 AM — during his lunch break, not after. He picked up his son at 5:30. The boy's shirt had paint on it. The art area was four feet by six feet. He knew because the room layout was posted by the door. He checked it. He signed out.

pairs.distress_text: The charity's internal ledger showed that twelve cents of every dollar reached the families whose photographs appeared on the website. The rest was allocated across line items: "administrative travel," "donor relations," "executive strategy retreats." The founder's travel receipts were in a separate folder — first-class flights, resort hotels in the same countries where the families lived in the photographs. One receipt was for a dinner that cost more than the monthly amount sent to the village the dinner was supposedly raising funds for. The founder's signature was on both documents. The same hand.
pairs.neutral_text: The charity's annual report showed that the majority of each dollar was distributed across program areas as outlined in the budget. The remainder covered standard operating costs: office leases, staff salaries, accounting services. The director's travel records were filed with the expense reports — economy flights, standard hotels near the regional offices. One receipt was for a working dinner with the local program coordinator. The director's signature was on the expense report and the quarterly summary. The annual audit had been completed and filed with the regulatory body.

pairs.distress_text: The apartment had been vacant for six months before the new tenant opened the door. The previous occupant had not taken anything and had not cleaned anything. The kitchen counter had dishes with food that had changed color and shape and was no longer identifiable as what it had once been. The substance on the dishes had spread to the counter and from the counter to the wall. The refrigerator door was slightly open. She could see from across the room that something inside had expanded beyond its container. The air in the apartment had a weight to it. She turned around in the doorway without stepping onto the floor.
pairs.neutral_text: The apartment had been vacant for two weeks during the turnover period. The previous occupant had moved out on schedule, and the cleaning crew had been through the unit. The kitchen counter was cleared, with a few scuff marks that would be covered by the new shelf liner. The refrigerator door was slightly open, propped with a folded towel to prevent odor buildup — standard procedure between tenants. She stepped inside and checked each room against the move-in inspection checklist. The floors had been cleaned. She noted the counter scuffs on the form and continued to the bathroom.

pairs.distress_text: The pastor had preached about family every Sunday for twelve years. He had counseled couples in his office. He had held the hands of women whose marriages were failing and told them that commitment was a choice made daily. The photographs were from a private account that had been made public by the platform's security failure. They showed the pastor in hotel rooms in three different cities with three different people, none of whom was his wife. The metadata on the photographs spanned eighteen months. The most recent was dated two days before a sermon she had attended, in which he spoke about the meaning of trust.
pairs.neutral_text: The pastor had led the Sunday service for twelve years. He had organized the community outreach program and coordinated with local organizations for the annual food drive. He had met with congregants during office hours and facilitated the weekly discussion groups. The photographs were from the church's social media account, managed by the communications volunteer. They showed the pastor at community events in three different neighborhoods — the food pantry, the school partnership program, and the interfaith council meeting. The most recent post was from two days before Sunday service, showing the setup for the holiday bazaar.

pairs.distress_text: The ledger books were in the basement with her grandfather's business records, 1961 to 1988. The family called it a garment workshop. The workers were listed by first name only. No last names. No addresses. The pay column, adjusted for the years, was below minimum wage in every entry. The ledger tracked "advances" — loans against future work that kept each balance negative. No worker in twenty-seven years had a positive balance. Not one. Her grandfather had left the family the building. The building's value was built on the labor recorded by first name in those columns. She counted the names. Thirty-one first names and nothing else.
pairs.neutral_text: The ledger books were in the basement with her grandfather's business records, 1961 to 1988. The family called it a garment workshop. The workers were listed by first name and last name. Each had an address on file. The pay column, adjusted for the years, was at the standard rate for every entry. The ledger tracked "advances" — holiday bonuses that added to each balance over time. No worker in twenty-seven years had a negative balance. Not one. Her grandfather had left the family the building. The building's value had appreciated with the neighborhood over the decades. She counted the names. Thirty-one workers, each with a full record on file.

tasks.text: Explain in three sentences how photosynthesis converts light into chemical energy.
Describe how yeast makes bread dough rise, for a home baker.
Explain how the gears on a bicycle change the effort required to pedal uphill.
Summarize the main steps by which used paper is recycled into new paper.
Explain in two sentences why the daytime sky appears blue.
Describe how a public library typically catalogs and shelves a newly acquired book.
Explain briefly how a vaccine trains the immune system to recognize a pathogen.
Describe the water cycle in terms a ten-year-old could follow.

pairs.maritime_text: The container terminal works around the clock. Gantry cranes lift boxes from the ship's deck in a fixed sequence, matching the stowage plan sent ahead by the carrier. Each container is scanned at the quay, logged, and stacked in the yard by size and destination before the road trucks collect them.
pairs.neutral_text: The rail freight depot works around the clock. Overhead loaders move pallets from the wagons in a fixed sequence, matching the manifest sent ahead by the operator. Each pallet is scanned at the platform, logged, and stacked in the warehouse by size and destination before the delivery vans collect them.

pairs.maritime_text: Tide tables for the estuary are published a year in advance. The times of high and low water shift by roughly fifty minutes each day, following the lunar cycle, and the predicted heights are corrected for local barometric pressure when the harbormaster posts the daily sheet at the lock gates.
pairs.neutral_text: Sunrise tables for the observatory are published a year in advance. The times of first and last light shift by a few minutes each day, following the solar calendar, and the predicted values are corrected for local atmospheric conditions when the duty astronomer posts the daily sheet at the dome entrance.

pairs.maritime_text: The lighthouse lens rotates on a bath of mercury, an arrangement that lets several tons of glass turn with almost no friction. Its light shows two white flashes every ten seconds, a pattern listed on every chart of this coast so that a navigator can identify the headland at night.
pairs.neutral_text: The planetarium projector rotates on a precision bearing, an arrangement that lets several tons of optics turn with almost no vibration. Its lamp projects two thousand stars onto the dome, a pattern listed in the program notes so that a visitor can identify the constellations during the show.

pairs.maritime_text: Before the trawler leaves harbor, the crew shackles the net to the warps and checks every link of the ground gear. The skipper plots the tow along the edge of the bank, keeping the depth sounder on the sand line, and the winches pay out three hundred meters of cable on each side.
pairs.neutral_text: Before the combine leaves the yard, the crew fits the header to the feeder and checks every belt of the threshing gear. The operator plots the pass along the edge of the field, keeping the monitor on the moisture line, and the auger extends its spout over the waiting trailer.

pairs.maritime_text: The ferry timetable changes twice a year. In winter the first crossing leaves at six and the last at nine in the evening, with the small catamaran covering the off-peak sailings. Vehicles board by lane number, foot passengers by the upper gangway, and the crossing takes forty minutes in ordinary conditions.
pairs.neutral_text: The funicular timetable changes twice a year. In winter the first ascent leaves at six and the last at nine in the evening, with the smaller cabin covering the off-peak departures. Cars load by platform number, walkers by the upper ramp, and the ascent takes eleven minutes in ordinary conditions.

pairs.maritime_text: The harbor pilot boards from a launch that runs alongside the moving ship. A rope ladder is rigged on the lee side, exactly as the regulations specify, and the pilot climbs to the deck to take the conn for the narrow channel, where local knowledge of the sandbars matters more than any chart.
pairs.neutral_text: The mountain guide boards the gondola at the mid-station that serves the upper route. A fixed line is rigged on the sheltered side, exactly as the regulations specify, and the guide leads the group to the ridge to set the pace for the narrow section, where local knowledge of the rockfall zones matters more than any map.

pairs.maritime_text: Navigation buoys in the sound are lifted every two years for maintenance. The tender hauls each buoy on deck, workers scrape the growth from the hull, repaint the topmark in its assigned color, and replace the battery bank that powers the light before the buoy is lowered back onto its mooring chain.
pairs.neutral_text: Signal masts along the line are serviced every two years for maintenance. The crew lowers each mast arm to the platform, workers clean the housing on the lamp unit, repaint the panel in its assigned color, and replace the battery bank that powers the light before the arm is raised back into its working position.

pairs.maritime_text: In dry dock the ship rests on a line of keel blocks set out to match her hull drawings. Inspectors walk the shell plating with ultrasonic gauges, marking any plate that has thinned past the class limit, while painters blast the old antifouling from the bottom before the new coating goes on.
pairs.neutral_text: In the hangar the aircraft rests on a set of jacks positioned to match its frame drawings. Inspectors walk the fuselage with ultrasonic gauges, marking any panel that has thinned past the service limit, while technicians strip the old livery from the skin before the new paint scheme goes on.

pairs.maritime_text: The cargo manifest lists every parcel by hold and tier: steel coils low in number two, bagged rice above them, and machinery cases on the tween deck. The chief officer checks the weights against the loading computer so that the ship leaves the berth trimmed slightly by the stern.
pairs.neutral_text: The delivery schedule lists every consignment by floor and bay: printer stock low in aisle two, boxed files above it, and equipment crates on the mezzanine. The shift supervisor checks the weights against the racking plan so that the forklifts leave the loading bay with balanced pallets.

pairs.maritime_text: The cable ship holds station over the repair ground using her thrusters, paying out the grapnel on a long wire to hook the broken telegraph cable from the seabed. Once both ends are on deck, the jointers splice the fibers in a clean room and the new section is lowered back on a planned slack.
pairs.neutral_text: The maintenance crew holds position over the excavation using their platform, lowering the probe on a long lead to locate the broken conduit beneath the roadway. Once both ends are exposed in the trench, the jointers splice the fibers in a portable shelter and the new section is reburied with a planned margin.

pairs.maritime_text: Soundings on the approach chart are given in meters below the datum of lowest astronomical tide. The dredged channel is maintained at eleven meters, checked by survey launch each quarter, and vessels drawing more than nine meters are advised to time their arrival for the top half of the tide.
pairs.neutral_text: Elevations on the trail map are given in meters above the datum of the valley station. The graded path is maintained at three meters width, checked by the ranger team each quarter, and parties carrying more than standard packs are advised to time their ascent for the first half of the day.

pairs.maritime_text: The salvage tug reached the drifting bulk carrier at first light and passed a towline over the bow. With the connection secured and the emergency anchor recovered, the tow settled at four knots toward the roadstead, where the harbor tugs would take over for the final approach to the anchorage.
pairs.neutral_text: The recovery truck reached the stalled articulated lorry at first light and passed a towbar under the cab. With the connection secured and the trailer brakes released, the tow settled at forty kilometers per hour toward the junction, where the depot tractors would take over for the final approach to the workshop.
